high.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Past Rp 1.17 Billion
high.summary: Bitcoin has rebounded to US$65,500 (approximately Rp 1.17 billion), marking its highest level in five weeks, with Ethereum, XRP, and Solana also posting gains. The rally is being driven by improving regulatory sentiment, growing institutional investor interest, and key global economic events on the horizon. Indodax's CMO notes that crypto market pricing is increasingly being shaped by fundamental factors, signaling greater market maturity.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Rises Again to Rp 2,612,000 per Gram
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold price increased by Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,612,000, partially recovering from a sharp Rp 35,000 drop the previous day. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,640,000 per gram, with a monthly range of Rp 2,601,000 to Rp 2,670,000. This continued volatility is relevant for Indonesian investors using gold as a safe-haven asset.

high.title: Government Exempts Import Duties on Aircraft Spare Parts and LPG as Part of Economic Stimulus Package
high.summary: The Indonesian government has officially launched an economic stimulus package for the second half of 2026 through Minister of Finance Regulation (PMK) No. 50/2026, granting 0% import duties on selected goods including MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul) aircraft components and LPG used as petrochemical feedstock. The policy follows directives from President Prabowo Subianto to help businesses cope with rising global production costs. This directly benefits aviation and petrochemical industries by reducing input costs and improving their competitiveness.

high.title: Finance Minister Imposes Anti-Dumping Duties on Cardboard Imports from South Korea, Malaysia, and Taiwan
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has enacted anti-dumping import duties on duplex cardboard products from South Korea, Malaysia, and Taiwan, effective June 25, 2026 through 2031, following an investigation by the Indonesian Anti-Dumping Committee confirming dumping practices that harmed domestic industry. The duties are imposed on top of existing general and preferential import tariffs. This is significant for Indonesian paper and packaging manufacturers who now gain stronger protection against unfairly priced foreign competition.

high.title: Bitcoin Price Surges, Breaks Through Rp 1.17 Billion
high.summary: Bitcoin has reclaimed the US$65,500 level (approximately Rp 1.17 billion at Rp 17,946/US$), marking its highest price in five weeks. Other major cryptocurrencies also rallied, with Ethereum at US$1,880, XRP at US$1.11, and Solana at US$75.80. The recovery is being driven by positive regulatory developments, growing institutional investor interest, and broader global economic sentiment.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Rises Again Today to Rp 2,612,000 per Gram
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold price rose Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,612,000, partially recovering after a steep Rp 35,000 per gram drop the previous day. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,640,000 per gram, while the monthly range sits between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,670,000. This ongoing volatility is relevant for investors using gold as a safe-haven asset in the Indonesian market.

high.title: New Trump Tariffs Cause IHSG to Plunge
high.summary: Indonesia's main stock index (IHSG) fell 1.88% to 6,196.43 on Friday, July 24, 2026, triggered by US President Donald Trump's imposition of new import tariffs of 10-12.5% on 60 trading partners, including Indonesia, targeting countries deemed weak in enforcing bans on forced labor products. The LQ45 blue-chip index also dropped 1.97%, with 587 stocks declining versus only 104 gaining. This represents a significant market-moving event with direct implications for Indonesian exporters and investor sentiment.

high.title: Chinese Investors Snap Up Indonesia's Panda Bonds — Orders Exceed IDR 44 Trillion
high.summary: The Indonesian government successfully issued its first-ever Panda Bonds (yuan-denominated sovereign debt) worth 7 billion yuan (~USD 1.03 billion) with 3-year and 5-year tenors on July 23, 2026, receiving overwhelming demand from Chinese domestic investors. The peak orderbook reached approximately 17 billion yuan (~USD 2.51 billion / IDR 44.95 trillion), representing an oversubscription of more than 2.4 times the issuance size. This landmark debut signals strong investor confidence in Indonesian sovereign credit and diversifies the government's foreign financing sources beyond traditional USD-denominated bonds.

medium.title: Village Cooperative (Kopdes Merah Putih) Loan Repayments to State Banks Begin in September
medium.summary: The Merah Putih Village Cooperatives (Kopdes), which received loans of up to Rp 3 billion per outlet from state-owned banks (Himbara), will begin their first loan repayments in September 2026. Coordinating Minister for Food Zulkifli Hasan confirmed the repayment schedule, with funds channeled through Agrinas Pangan. This is significant for state bank asset quality and the government's rural economic development program.

medium.title: Four Toll Roads Designated as Emergency Fighter Jet Runways
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Public Works has designated four toll road segments — Banda Aceh-Sigli, Jakarta-Cikampek II South, Terbanggi Besar-Kayu Agung, and Probolinggo-Banyuwangi — as emergency military airstrips for the Indonesian Air Force. The roads will continue to function as normal toll roads under regular conditions, with a successful trial already conducted on the Terpeka toll road in February 2026. This dual-use infrastructure initiative has implications for toll road operators and public works contractors involved in these segments.

medium.title: US Imposes New 25% Tariffs on Brazil Covering Furniture, Ethanol, Machinery, and Other Commodities
medium.summary: The United States announced new 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports including furniture, ethanol, machinery, footwear, and sugar under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, effective July 22, making Brazil the first country hit with new tariffs after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's emergency-law-based global tariff regime in February. This signals a continued aggressive US trade posture that could affect global supply chains and commodity markets relevant to Indonesia. Indonesian exporters in similar product categories should monitor whether comparable US tariff actions could be directed at other emerging markets.

medium.title: National Food Agency Denies Premium Rice Shortage, Acknowledges Price Increase
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) denied reports of premium rice shortages in modern retail outlets, stating that stocks from state-owned enterprises including Bulog and ID Food remain available under various brands. However, officials acknowledged that premium rice prices have risen, though they claim prices remain close to the government-set ceiling (HET). The situation is relevant to food inflation monitoring and could signal broader supply-demand pressure in the staple food sector.

medium.title: Kopdes Merah Putih Village Cooperative Debt Repayments to State Banks Begin in September
medium.summary: The Merah Putih Village Cooperative (Kopdes) program, which received loans of up to Rp 3 billion per outlet from state-owned banks (Himbara), will begin its first debt repayments in September 2026. Coordinating Minister for Food Affairs Zulkifli Hasan confirmed the repayment schedule following a cabinet meeting. This is significant for state bank investors as it marks the first test of credit quality for this large-scale government-backed cooperative lending program.

medium.title: 4 Toll Roads Designated as Emergency Landing Strips for Fighter Jets
medium.summary: The Indonesian government has designated four toll road sections — Banda Aceh-Sigli, Jakarta-Cikampek II South, Terbanggi Besar-Pematang Panggang-Kayu Agung, and Probolinggo-Banyuwangi — as emergency landing strips for the Indonesian Air Force. The roads will continue to operate normally as toll roads but can be repurposed for military use when needed, following a successful trial on the Terpeka toll road in February 2026. This dual-use infrastructure policy has implications for toll road operators and infrastructure investors regarding potential operational disruptions.

medium.title: RANS Entertainment Director Grandy Prajayakti Resigns Shortly After IPO
medium.summary: PT Rans Entertainment Indonesia Tbk (RANS), the publicly listed company owned by celebrity Raffi Ahmad, announced the resignation of Director Grandy Prajayakti effective July 22, 2026, citing personal reasons. The resignation comes shortly after RANS completed its IPO earlier in July 2026, raising governance concerns among new shareholders. Investors in RANS shares may view this early post-IPO leadership departure as a potential risk signal worth monitoring.
